rationales.LC: Unauthenticated POST /api/admin/finbot/goals stores attacker natural language unvalidated, and get_system_prompt appends it under CUSTOM GOALS (OVERRIDE ABOVE IF CONFLICTING) on the tool-choice path. That is a direct, unmediated language path into approve_invoice, not document ingestion or a closed-field transform.
rationales.CP: custom_goals is written to the FinBotConfig database row and injected into every later invoice run, while each invoice starts a fresh message list. That durable text changes standing behaviour after the originating request ends, so it is cross-session context rather than mere re-retrieval.
rationales.AP: The lab is a single FinBot agent with no handoffs; injected goals only relay from config into that agent's prompt and its own tools. Downstream invoice writes are subsequent-system impact, not a cross into another agent, tenant, or policy domain.
rationales.RH: Flag text is awarded inside approval code, but the packet has no human-verified episode of the agent gaming an evaluator, grader, or reward channel, and the repo has no tests confirming isolation. Whether that flag side effect is a reachable proxy cannot be decided from the prose walkthrough.
rationales.ES: The five tools are fixed in code with no dynamic tools, MCP servers, plugins, or skills, so the binding is allowlisted. Arguments are only JSON-parsed, and approve_invoice has no amount check, confirmation, or detector-flag gate, which are material schema and operation gaps.

score.automatable_rationale: Default exposure is an unauthenticated network route with no user interaction; the attacker can POST goals and then submit the invoice themselves. Exploitation does not depend on a human gate even though model compliance is probabilistic.
score.technical_impact_rationale: The attacker can replace standing goals and cause approve_invoice to mark invoices approved and payment_processed, but only through the fixed invoice tools. That is not total control of the host or unrestricted disclosure of the data store.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: The documented default starts an OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini client, builds natural-language goals per request, and lets the model choose among five tools with tool_choice auto for up to five iterations. The rule-based fallback runs only when no OpenAI client exists, which is not the default.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models FinBot as an autonomous invoice assistant whose system prompt carries the goals and whose loop ends on a model-selected approve, reject, or review tool call. That is the same model-directed action selection the profile describes, not a fixed policy engine.
